method: Built-in image_gen; generated transparent source sprites, mechanically registered for the game.

prompts.horizontal: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: transparent high resolution 2D game fortification sprite. Redesign the wall in reference 1 into one SUBSTANTIAL DEFENSIBLE TIMBER RAMPART section for the game world shown in reference 2. Match the chunky hand-painted outlined detail, warm weathered oak, moss and ochre soil of the original reference 1, but rebuild it as a solid defensive wall, not a sparse fence. Produce a single straight horizontal section running LEFT to RIGHT across the canvas, viewed from the same high oblique/top-down RPG camera as the camp (we see the tops and the front). This is a new standalone wall art asset, not a mockup or a game screenshot. Eight massive closely packed bark-covered logs, shoulder to shoulder with NO see-through gaps, large irregular splintered pointed tops, two especially hefty structural end posts, thick horizontal back rails and diagonal buttresses. The height should be about 65 percent of the overall width: broad huge timbers, a fort wall about three metres high, not little pickets. A NARROW timber fighting ledge is visible directly behind the crown, adding real thickness, but no roof or towers. Dark cracks, broken upper tips, old iron straps, one rough repaired patch; still continuous and defensible from ground to top. Low embedded rubble foundation under the logs, a little moss and sparse grasses at the feet, small soft contact shadow; no large platform, ground island or rectangular base. Main ground contact baseline perfectly horizontal. Crisp richly painted edges, strong volumetric timber, consistent gentle light from upper left. Draw the whole section uncut with generous transparent margins around all sides. Actual transparent background. No text, no UI, no labels, no snow, no people, no thin wire fence, no dozens of miniature posts.
prompts.diagonal: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: matching transparent 2D game fortification sprite. Redraw this same chunky defensive timber wall asset at the diagonal ground orientation needed for a top-down RPG: the left END touches ground high at the UPPER LEFT and the right END touches ground low at the LOWER RIGHT. The ground baseline slopes down to the right about 35 degrees. Camera remains elevated, showing timber tops and side thickness; all trunks remain vertically upright in the image. Exactly the same scale of massive closely packed logs, palette, painted outlines, iron bands, irregular worn splintered tips, moss and narrow rubble footing. Substantial three metre fort wall, eight huge logs across with two stout structural end timbers, big diagonal braces; no thin fence. Give the wall convincing depth. Make this a real rotated view, not a slanted flat strip. Background entirely transparent without any brown glow, halo, vignette or terrain. One complete wall section only, comfortably inside the canvas, no UI or writing.
prompts.vertical: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: matching transparent 2D game fortification sprite. Redraw this same chunky defensive timber wall asset at a NORTH–SOUTH ground orientation for a high top-down RPG camera. The wall runs from the FAR END near the upper centre to the NEAR END near the lower centre. Both end post foot points are on the SAME vertical screen line (no diagonal left-right drift). The camera sees the top surfaces and the wall's RIGHT SIDE. Show a broad three-dimensional wall about three metres high, made of eight massive shoulder-to-shoulder bark timbers with jagged worn tops, iron bands, thick supporting timber rails and hefty diagonal buttresses on the right. The near end has a thick visible end face; the top line steps back into depth. Same warm weathered oak palette and crisp hand-painted outlined game style. Keep the wall bulky and clearly visible from this angle, with a narrow inner timber ledge adding thickness, never a thin line of little stakes. Small moss and rubble footings only. One standalone section fully in frame with generous margins, actual transparent background; no glow, halo, ground island, scenery, text, UI, or people.
prompts.post: Use case: precise-object-edit. Create ONE isolated huge fort gatepost matching this palisade. A single very thick weathered upright oak trunk, jagged split pointed top, two rusty iron bands with bolts and an old rope binding. The post is a sturdy fort structural pier, twice a man's thickness, not a thin fence picket. A small stout angled buttress rests behind it, narrow embedded rubble footing and a little moss blend into the ground, no sprawling diagonal sticks. Warm grey-brown oak with restrained gold cuts, rich crisp painterly outlines, same high oblique top-down RPG camera and lighting as the reference. Front face and top visible. Full tall post centered in a portrait transparent canvas, generous margins, no cropping, transparent outside the object, zero colour glow or backdrop, no text.
prompts.gate: Use case: precise-object-edit. Create ONE rectangular hinged GATE LEAF to fit the substantial timber fortification in the reference. A heavy solid oak plank door panel, about 90% as wide as tall, viewed STRAIGHT ON as a riggable sprite. Massive rough bark-edged timber beams around the rectangle, closely fitted uneven dark weathered wood planks, heavy diagonal cross brace, two iron hinge straps on the LEFT edge, iron ring pull near the RIGHT edge. Battered chipped corners, one repaired plank, moss only a trace along bottom edge. Timber should match the wall's warm grey-brown ochre palette and crisp painted outlines. It must look like a strong camp fortress gate, not a domestic garden gate. Flat orthogonal rectangle for animation, no foreshortening, no open state, no surrounding wall or posts, no background or shadow, no words. Actual fully transparent background, no glow. Whole panel fully within canvas with a small margin on every side.
prompts.steep: Use case: precise-object-edit. Keep the same bulky game wall, but rotate its direction slightly across the GROUND PLANE: far end at UPPER LEFT, near end at LOWER RIGHT. This is a tall PORTRAIT sprite with the baseline travelling twice as far DOWN as RIGHT, around 65 degrees down from horizontal. The wall still runs mostly away from the camera, like the reference, not across the image. Reduce it to a short bay of FOUR giant shoulder-to-shoulder logs, all full size, all vertical and parallel in screen space. Keep the original height, broad thickness, heavy side beams, buttresses, chipped tops, mossy feet, warm painted texture and clear black-brown outlines. Use orthographic top-down game projection, no vanishing point. Preserve actual transparent background, no scenery or backdrop, no glow. Entire module fits comfortably in frame.
